title: Co-Lipschitz bounds pass to the derivative at density points
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, B ⊆ ℝ^n any set, m > 0 and b ∈ ℝ^n. Assume (i) m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| for every a ∈ B; (ii) F is differentiable at b; (iii) λ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺, where λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n used as an outer measure and the quotient lies in [0,∞]. Then m|c| ≤ |DF(b)c| for every c ∈ ℝ^n.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℝ) (b : Euclid n), 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖F a - F b‖) → DifferentiableAt ℝ F b → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => volume (B ∩ closedBall b ρ) / volume (closedBall b ρ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → ∀ c : Euclid n, m * ‖c‖ ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ F b c‖
